ds.title: Privacy policy (Datenschutz)
s: Milen Yakimov, Cleverhoferweg 154, 23611 Bad Schwartau, Germany, email: {MAIL}

This website sets no cookies and uses no advertising services. We use GoatCounter to count visits anonymously (see section 4). What you type into the letter templates stays in your browser and is not sent to us or to third parties.

The website is served via GitHub Pages, a service of GitHub, Inc., 88 Colin P. Kelly Jr. St., San Francisco, CA 94107, USA. When pages are accessed, GitHub processes technically necessary data, in particular your IP address, which according to GitHub is logged and stored for security purposes. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR; our legitimate interest is the secure and reliable operation of the website. Data may be transferred to the USA; according to GitHub, it participates in the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework. Details in GitHub's privacy statement: {GH}

To see how many people use the website and which pages are helpful, we use the GoatCounter service (goatcounter.com). A small script is loaded from gc.zgo.at. It records, for example, the page visited, the previous website (referrer), browser and device type, screen size and approximate country. No cookies are set, no data is stored on your device and no user profiles are created; the statistics are anonymous. What you type into the letter templates is not recorded. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR; our legitimate interest is improving the service. If you use an ad blocker, counting usually does not take place. Details: {GC}

On the “Translate a letter” page, uploaded photos, PDFs and texts are processed only in your browser; they are not sent to us and not stored. For text recognition your browser loads program files and language data from jsDelivr (cdn.jsdelivr.net) and, for PDFs, from Cloudflare cdnjs (cdnjs.cloudflare.com); this technically transmits your IP address to these providers, but not your letter. Translation is done, where your browser supports it, with the browser's built-in translation on your device. Only if you choose the link “Open in Google Translate” yourself is the recognised text sent to Google; Google's privacy terms then apply. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR.

When you choose a language, federal state, city or health insurer, this choice is saved in your browser's local storage so you don't have to choose it again next time. This storage is necessary for the service you requested (§ 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG). It is not sent to us, and you can delete it at any time in your browser settings.
If you email us, we process your details only to answer your request (Art. 6(1)(b) or (f) GDPR) and delete them once they are no longer needed.

You have the right to access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, data portability and to object (Art. 15–21 GDPR). You can also complain to a data protection supervisory authority, for example the Independent Centre for Privacy Protection Schleswig-Holstein (ULD), Kiel.
